findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the rework-signal shapes: only attempts_per_ticket is per-ticket (dict[str,int]); revert_recovery/reopen_recovery/first_pass_rate ship as repo-wide scalars — either scope per-ticket derivations from their underlying STATUS/reverts scans or restrict the per-ticket correlation to attempts_per_ticket + caused_by fan-in + patchset count.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:242 def revert_recovery(...) -> int (repo-wide count, `return count`)
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:272 def reopen_recovery(...) -> int (repo-wide count)
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:292 first_pass_rate(...) -> float | None (single fraction over all tickets)
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:162 attempts_per_ticket(...) -> dict[str, int] — the ONLY per-ticket-shaped signal
Plan: 'ticket-level proxies already shipped in rebar metrics (attempts_per_ticket, revert_recovery, reopen_recovery, first_pass_rate)'
findings.finding: The per-ticket correlation mechanism cannot consume three of the four cited rework signals: revert_recovery and reopen_recovery return a single repo-wide int, and first_pass_rate returns a single float — only attempts_per_ticket is per-ticket (dict[str,int]). The plan calls all four 'ticket-level proxies already shipped' and correlates the per-ticket shape row 'against the per-ticket rework signals', but three of them expose no per-ticket value to join on.
findings.location: Approach -> Read (a), 'Rework signals, in order of cost' and 'The join key, explicitly' ('correlates against the per-ticket rework signals')
scenarios: Implementer wires the correlation to revert_recovery(repo_root) and gets a single scalar, with no per-ticket vector to align to the per-ticket shape rows
findings.suggested_fix: State that attempts_per_ticket is the per-ticket count proxy joined directly, and that revert/reopen presence is derived per-ticket by reusing the same STATUS-edge / state['reverts'] scans those scalars are built from (yielding a per-ticket boolean/count), rather than calling the shipped repo-wide scalar functions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the reports/stability/ un-ignore prerequisite an explicit depends_on edge on yogic-soapstone-takin (f9b9-83ad-931c-4833) rather than a narrative stack assertion, so the reports are guaranteed committable when this task runs.
evidence: 'reports/ is gitignored; the .gitignore re-inclusion of reports/stability/ lands in sibling yogic-soapstone-takin (f9b9-83ad-931c-4833), which sits below this change in the stack. This task inherits it'
AC1/AC3/AC4 verified by git ls-files reports/stability/…
findings.finding: AC1/AC3/AC4 require reports under reports/stability/ to be tracked (git ls-files), but reports/ is gitignored and the .gitignore re-inclusion of reports/stability/ lands in sibling yogic-soapstone-takin. The plan asserts a narrative stack ordering ('sits below this change in the stack') rather than a stated depends_on edge; if the ordering isn't enforced, git add of the reports silently no-ops and the ACs cannot be satisfied.
scenarios: Sibling has not merged / is reordered above this ticket; the report files match the ignore rule and are never added; git ls-files returns empty and AC1/AC3/AC4 fail at verification
findings.suggested_fix: Add the formal dependency edge and cite it in the Dependency section so the git ls-files ACs are provable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a focused unit test for the new join/aggregation logic — assert group_by_ticket SUMs per-commit shape and unions files, and that a commit with an ambiguous 4-quad or absent trailer is excluded from the correlation and its UNJOINABLE count reported.
evidence: 'A commit whose trailer does not resolve to exactly one full canonical id ... is UNJOINABLE: it is excluded from the correlation and its count is reported, never silently dropped.'
'the existing pinned-corpus self-check still passes, proving the all-work extension did not perturb the shipped bug-corpus path' — this covers the OLD path, not the new join/aggregation logic.

'Measurement reads are evidence documents ... their oracle is reproducibility (AC2) rather than a new automated test' — but the join/aggregation code is in-process pure logic with correctness stakes, not a measurement read.
findings.finding: The all-work extension adds net-new conditional logic — the group_by_ticket SUM/union aggregation and the UNJOINABLE classification (ambiguous 4-quad fragment, ticket no longer present) — but the Testing section provides no direct unit test for it; the pinned-corpus self-check only proves the OLD bug-corpus path is unperturbed, and the all-work 'reproduce n' oracle is an end-to-end reproducibility check on real data, not an assertion that a commit with an ambiguous or absent trailer is correctly excluded and counted.
findings.location: Testing section; Approach 'The join key, explicitly'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small fixture-based test exercising group_by_ticket (SUM of non-test LOC/total LOC/commit count, file union) and the UNJOINABLE path (ambiguous fragment and absent-ticket cases), independent of the real-corpus reproduce-n check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that `group_by_ticket` is a NEW helper created by this task (not a shipped symbol) and specify its aggregation contract inline (SUM non-test LOC / total LOC / commit count, union files-touched, keyed on the first `rebar-ticket:` trailer resolved via extract_ticket_refs).
evidence: Plan text: 'Commits fold into tickets with `group_by_ticket`, which SUMS the per-commit shape variables into per-ticket aggregates ... and unions files-touched'
Grep for 'def group_by_ticket' and 'group_by_ticket' across the repo: (no matches)

Contrast: sibling helpers cited the same way DO exist — extract_ticket_refs (src/rebar/_commands/verify_commit.py:57), count_non_test_diff_lines and escalation_for_diff (imported in scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py:58-62)
The plan's File impact lists scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py as 'extend', which is where a new group_by_ticket would live
findings.finding: The aggregation helper `group_by_ticket` is named in monospace as though it is a shipped mechanism, but no such symbol exists anywhere in the repo; it is ambiguous whether the plan claims it already ships or intends to create it as part of the extend scope.
scenarios: An implementer reads the monospace name as an existing import and greps for it, finding nothing, then stalls or guesses at its contract
findings.suggested_fix: State in the Approach that `group_by_ticket` is added by the script extension (File impact already lists scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py as 'extend'), and drop the monospace/shipped framing that pairs it with the genuinely-imported helpers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the correlation/relationship method for read (a) (e.g. Spearman rank on each variable vs the ordered rework signals) so the reported relationship is reproducible and method-stable.
evidence: 'measuring rework against three variables'
AC1: 'each one's measured relationship to rework'
No correlation statistic named; the 2026 grounding notes nonstationarity but the read protocol does not fix a method
findings.finding: AC1/read(a) requires 'each one's measured relationship to rework' but the statistical method for computing that relationship is unspecified (Pearson vs Spearman vs bucketed rework-rate). With ordinal cost-ordered rework signals and count variables (files touched, commit fragmentation), the method materially changes the result and is left to the executor.
scenarios: Executor picks Pearson on rank-skewed count data and reports a misleading coefficient
Reviewer of the report cannot tell whether the reported relationship used a rank or linear measure
findings.suggested_fix: Name the default in the Method section, e.g. 'Spearman rank correlation per variable against each rework signal, with n reported inline.'

evidence: 5 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the Gerrit auth/HTTPS precondition for the `o=ALL_REVISIONS` patchset-count read: which credentials it uses, that it hits the `/a/` authenticated namespace over HTTPS with basic auth (and strips the XSSI prefix), and whether it reuses `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` or a new stdlib call.
evidence: Plan quote: 'patchset count from Gerrit `o=ALL_REVISIONS`, which is the cheapest per-change rework proxy and the only one requiring the network.'

The shipped Gerrit REST client (src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:9-11) documents the precondition the plan omits: 'All authenticated REST calls hit the /a/ (authenticated) namespace with HTTP basic auth (BOT_USER:GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN)' and strips the XSSI `)]}'` prefix; it already issues `o=CURRENT_REVISION` at gerrit_client.py:266, so `o=ALL_REVISIONS` is a Partially-verified surface on the same endpoint family.

ABSENCE: neither the Approach, Dependency, nor Testing sections name credentials, the `/a/` authenticated namespace, HTTPS/basic-auth, or whether the backtest reuses GerritClient vs. rolls its own urllib call.
Evidence class: Partially-verified (endpoint family used; specific ALL_REVISIONS query path and the script's auth wiring unconfirmed).
findings.finding: The plan depends on a networked Gerrit REST read (patchset count via `o=ALL_REVISIONS`, explicitly 'the only one requiring the network') but states no auth/HTTPS precondition for it.
findings.location: Approach — Read (a): 'patchset count from Gerrit `o=ALL_REVISIONS` ... the only one requiring the network'; File impact: scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py
scenarios: The extended backtest is run in an environment without GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN / bot credentials and every patchset-count read returns HTTP 401/403, silently degrading the per-change rework proxy to zero-coverage.
The script issues the read against the unauthenticated (non-`/a/`) namespace or over plain HTTP and gets a different (or XSSI-guarded, unparsed) body than the reviewer expects.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach Read (a), add that the patchset-count read reuses the shipped `GerritClient` (src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py) so it inherits the `/a/`-namespace + `BOT_USER:GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` basic-auth over HTTPS and XSSI-stripping, and note in Testing/AC2 that read (a)'s reproducible-n claim covers the local git-derived shape variables while the network patchset-count column degrades gracefully (reported as unavailable) when credentials are absent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the degraded-mode behavior for the Gerrit patchset-count read: on fetch failure, fall back to the offline rework proxies and record in the report's Method section that the network proxy was unavailable, rather than aborting or silently emitting blanks.
evidence: 'patchset count from Gerrit o=ALL_REVISIONS, which is the cheapest per-change rework proxy and the only one requiring the network.'
No error-handling or degraded-mode statement for a Gerrit fetch failure anywhere in the plan; AC2 requires the reported n be reproducible, which a silent network failure could perturb.
findings.finding: Read (a)'s cheapest-network rework proxy (Gerrit patchset count via o=ALL_REVISIONS) is an external call the plan flags as 'the only one requiring the network', but the plan does not state what the script does if that Gerrit read fails or is unreachable — whether it degrades to the offline proxies (attempts_per_ticket / caused_by fan-in) and records the degradation, or aborts.
findings.location: Approach, Read (a) — 'patchset count from Gerrit o=ALL_REVISIONS ... the only one requiring the network'
